lessonRef.unitTitle: PF4 — Using Credit: Debt Strategy and Repayment Analysis
lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: refinancing, consolidation, and their tradeoffs

objective: Evaluate a fictional refinance offer by computing its break-even point and its net saving, and identify the condition under which the offer fails despite the lower rate.
scenario: Cornelius Iyengar-Mbatha has been offered the simulated refinance below. The lender, balance, rates, and fees are invented for this exercise.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional refinance terms in these directions

tasks.directions: The current loan has a $16,800 balance at 11.2% a year, with 42 payments of $485.35 left. The refinance offer keeps the same 42-month term and the same balance at 7.6% a year, with payments of $456.81, and charges $625 in fees at the start. Monthly interest is the annual rate divided by 12.

prompts.text: How much interest does the current loan charge in its first month, at 11.2% a year?
How much interest would the refinanced loan charge in its first month, at 7.6% a year?
How much lower is the monthly payment under the refinance?

tasks.directions: Now test whether the offer is worth its fees.

prompts.text: How many months of the monthly saving does it take to recover the $625 in fees? Give one decimal place.
What is the total of payments under the current loan?
What is the total of payments under the refinance?
What is the net saving from refinancing across the full 42 months, after the $625 in fees?
Cornelius expects to repay the loan early, in about 18 months. Do the $625 of fees get recovered out of the monthly payment saving by then?
choices: Yes, the payment saving covers the fees by month 18
No, the payment saving has not covered the fees by month 18

tasks.directions: Answer each in a few sentences.

prompts.text: The refinance cuts the rate from 11.2% to 7.6% and can still be the wrong choice. Explain the mechanism, state the condition that decides it, and say what Cornelius should establish about his own plans before accepting.
The first month’s interest falls by $50.40 but the payment falls by only $28.54. Explain where the other $21.86 goes, and why that is not a loss to Cornelius.

remediation: If the refinance looks like a clear win, check whether the $625 of fees has been included. The gross saving is $1,198.68 across 42 months, but the fees are paid at the start and come off that, leaving $573.68. Compute the break-even in months first, then compare it against how long the loan is actually expected to run.
extension: Find the largest fee at which the refinance would still break even by month 18, and say how far that is from the $625 charged.
